findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the store-compat unit becomes re-stampable and conditional: derive the desired required_capabilities from the project mapping's project count, re-write/commit the record when the committed set differs (not only when absent), and add multi-project-bridge to KNOWN_CAPABILITIES so the writing binary passes its own gate.
evidence: _store_compat_unit commits only on absent blob: `if _git(tracker, "show", f"tickets:{compat.COMPAT_FILENAME}").returncode == 0: return EnsureOutcome(... "ok")` (init.py:522-523)
KNOWN_CAPABILITIES is empty and any required cap fails the gate closed (compat.py:60, _analyze:284-293)
Criterion 7 requires a store whose mapping holds >1 project to CARRY multi-project-bridge while a single-project store remains writable — implying re-stamping on transitions in both directions
findings.finding: The store-compat 'conditional capability stamp' child does not address that the existing store-compat ensure unit only writes the record when the committed blob is ABSENT (tree-check -> ok) and never re-stamps a converged store, nor that KNOWN_CAPABILITIES is currently empty; as written the mechanism cannot add multi-project-bridge when a store gains a second project after the record already exists, nor remove it on the reverse transition, and a binary writing the capability would fail its own gate.
findings.location: Scope: src/rebar/_store/compat.py — the conditional capability stamp; child 'Store-compat capability stamp'; AC line 7
scenarios: A store that already has .store-compat.json then adds a second project via `bridge projects set`: the ensure unit's absent-blob tree-check short-circuits to `ok` and never adds the capability, so an older binary is NOT fenced out — the exact duplicate-in-wrong-project failure the criterion exists to prevent.
A store dropping back to one project needs the capability REMOVED so older binaries regain access; an absent-only stamp never removes it.
The current binary writing multi-project-bridge would itself hit StoreIncompatibleError because that cap is not in KNOWN_CAPABILITIES.
findings.suggested_fix: Change _store_compat_unit's check-then-act from 'blob absent' to 'committed required_capabilities != desired set computed from the mapping', add `multi-project-bridge` to KNOWN_CAPABILITIES, and have write_compat_record accept/compute the capability list; cover both the add (>1 project) and remove (back to <=1) transitions in the store-compat test.

findings.finding: The multi-project inbound fetch child scopes JQL fan-out and the truncation ceiling per project but does not address the three per-project enrichment passes the current fetcher runs (get_parent_map / get_comment_map / get_issuelinks_map), each of which takes exactly one project key; fanning out the base JQL while leaving enrichment single-project silently drops inbound parent/comment/issuelink data for every project but one.
findings.location: Child decomposition — 'Multi-project inbound fetch'; vs src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py:593-718 (_build_snapshot enrichment)
findings.suggested_fix: Have _build_snapshot iterate the configured project set for the enrichment step too — call get_parent_map/get_comment_map/get_issuelinks_map once per project and merge each result — and add the multi-project enrichment fidelity to the two-project fetch acceptance test.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion covering the ticket repos field and inbound repo-defaulting from the mapping (e.g. an ingested ticket records the repos derived from its project's mapping entry).
evidence: Child: 'Ticket repos field — schema, reducer, create-time arg, inbound defaulting from the mapping.'
None of the seven Acceptance Criteria mention the repos field or inbound repo defaulting.
findings.finding: The 'Ticket repos field' child (schema, reducer, create-time arg, inbound defaulting from the mapping) has no covering acceptance criterion — no AC asserts the repos field is written, read, or defaulted from the mapping.
findings.location: Child decomposition — 'Ticket repos field'; Acceptance Criteria
scenarios: Inbound defaulting from the mapping ships untested and could silently mis-associate tickets to repos.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC: 'An ingested ticket records the repo set derived from its project's mapping entry; checked by a reconciler test asserting the repos field on a created ticket matches the mapping.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion verifying the promote-only rule: changing the project of a bound ticket is rejected while setting a project on an unbound (absent-project) ticket succeeds.
evidence: Child: '...promote-only rule (cannot change project of a bound ticket). Delivers empty-project criterion.'
The cited empty-project criterion (AC line 3) verifies no-outbound-for-empty, not the promote-only/reject-change behavior.
findings.finding: The promote-only rule ('cannot change project of a bound ticket') under the Ticket project field child has no covering acceptance criterion, so the invariant is described but never verified.
scenarios: A caller attempts to change the project of an already-bound ticket; nothing in CI asserts the change is rejected.

findings.finding: The 'Ticket repos field' child delivers substantive functional work — schema, reducer, create-time arg, and inbound defaulting of repos from the mapping — but no acceptance criterion covers it. The 'two new ticket fields' are in Scope, yet only the project field is verified (AC3 empty-project, AC4 explicit-project); the repos field and its mapping-driven inbound defaulting have no covering criterion.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria / Child decomposition — 'Ticket repos field'
findings.suggested_fix: Add: 'An inbound ticket with no explicit repos records the repos derived from the store mapping for its project; checked by a reconciler test asserting the recorded repos on an ingested ticket match the mapping entry.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend child 1734's scope and acceptance criteria to fan the three enrichment passes (get_parent_map/get_comment_map/get_issuelinks_map) across every configured project and merge results into the shared snapshot, with a test asserting both projects' enrichment data present — matching parent AC2.
evidence: Parent AC2 (current description): 'checked by a reconciler test asserting one JQL pair AND one enrichment pass (parent/comment/issuelink maps) is issued per configured project, with both projects' enrichment data present in the merged snapshot'.

Parent decomposition, Multi-project inbound fetch bullet: 'the three per-project enrichment passes (get_parent_map / get_comment_map / get_issuelinks_map) also fan across every configured project — one call per project, results merged into the shared snapshot keyed by issue ... Enrichment fidelity joins the two-project fetch acceptance test.'

Child 1734's five ACs cover: JQL pair per project, source-project+repos recording, per-project truncation ceiling, single-project regression, zero-issue project — NONE mentions enrichment/get_parent_map/get_comment_map/get_issuelinks_map.

fetcher.py:597-600 calls client.get_parent_map(project_key) with a single project_key; the enrichment merge in _build_snapshot is single-project today, so it would 'silently drop parent/comment/issuelink data for every project but one' (parent's own words) unless fanned out.

Sibling a33c (size relief) extracts only the pagination cluster (_iter_pages/collect/_ACLI_CEILING/SilentTruncationError) and explicitly leaves the enrichment merge in fetcher._build_snapshot; it is behaviour-preserving and delivers no criterion. No other sibling touches the enrichment merge.
findings.finding: Parent acceptance criterion 2 requires that 'one enrichment pass (parent/comment/issuelink maps) is issued per configured project, with both projects' enrichment data present in the merged snapshot' — but the multi-project inbound fetch child (1734) covers only the JQL-pair fan-out and source-project recording; its acceptance criteria say nothing about the three per-project enrichment passes. No sibling covers the enrichment remainder, so this half of AC2 is uncovered.
scenarios: A store with two projects fetches: the enrichment merge runs once with one project_key, so parent/comment/issuelink data for the second project is dropped from the merged snapshot even though the child ships and its ACs pass — the parent's completion verifier for AC2 (both projects' enrichment data present) then fails.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an acceptance criterion to child 1734 asserting one enrichment call per configured project for each of get_parent_map/get_comment_map/get_issuelinks_map with both projects' data merged into the snapshot, and add the enrichment merge site (fetcher._build_snapshot:577-685) to its scope; this also closes the G4 owned-by-none gap on the enrichment merge that both 1734 and a33c touch but neither owns.
